newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar ends barely changed after tight range.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends barely changed after tight range.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar ended little-changed after a quiet Friday session but had the potential to push higher next week, dealers said.

If interest rates remained high and if the flow of dual currency issues continued, then the Kiwi could expect support, but much would depend on what emerges from ongoing coalition talks between the major parties after last month's inconclusive general election.
The Kiwi ended at US$0.7070/77 and at 67.59 on the Trade-Weighted Index, almost exactly level with the opening, after trading a tight 0.7063-76 range.

One Auckland dealer said selling pressure from Asia had dissipated. "While these yields continue to stick around, on a 90-day basis, at the 9.0 percent level, and the swap spreads remain where they are, it is still attractive for these offshore guys," he said.
"I think it will be in a range of 0.7045 up to 0.7150. We may re-test these old highs. It depends on what sort of feedback we get from these coalition talks as well," he said.
